claims.claim: Daikin's integrated hybrid selects heat source on energy prices (Economical) or primary energy (Ecological); the choice is field setting [7-04].
claims.quote: Set to Economical, the system will in all operating conditions select the energy source (gas or electricity) based on energy prices, resulting in a minimisation of energy costs.

claims.claim: The Ecological mode uses a fixed primary energy factor for electricity of 2.5 (40% generation efficiency), gas = 1.
claims.quote: Assuming an average electricity production efficiency (including transportation losses) of 40%, the primary energy factor for electricity equals 2.5 (=1/0.40).

claims.claim: With a third-party boiler, switching is a temperature rule: a bivalent ON temperature Tcalc, bounded by [C-03] and [C-03]+[C-04], with a fixed 3 C hysteresis; prices enter only through the installer's choice of [C-03].
claims.quote: Tcalc Bivalent ON temperature (variable). Below this temperature, the gas boiler will always be ON. Tcalc can never go below [C-03] or above [C-03]+[C-04].

claims.claim: The installer derives [C-03] from a static break-even COP = (electricity price / gas price) x boiler efficiency; worked example gives COP 3 and [C-03] = 2.5 at LWT 35 C.
claims.quote: COP = (Electricity price / gas price) x boiler efficiency
claims.locator: s.11 Configuration, 'Bivalent', p.163; example: 20 c/kWh electricity, 6 c/kWh gas, efficiency 0.9 gives COP 3; graph note a: [C-03]=2.5 in case of COP=3 and LWT=35 C

claims.claim: The householder-facing logic is a price comparison; it depends on the user keeping static gas and electricity prices up to date (up to three electricity price levels on a timer).
claims.quote: Dependent on your energy prices the unit will automatically either run the heat pump only, bring on the boiler to assist the heat pump, or run the boiler only.

claims.claim: Prices are entered manually and must be re-entered after a tariff change.
claims.quote: If your system mode is set to economical, you will be able to change your energy prices.

claims.quote: 'bivalent temperature' (Tbiv) means the outdoor temperature declared by the manufacturer for heating at which the declared capacity for heating equals the part load for heating and below which the declared capacity for heating requires supplementary capacity

claims.claim: MIS 3005-D (Dec 2024) admits hybrids: heat pump sized to at least 55% of design heat load at 55 C flow.
claims.quote: The requirement that the heat pump shall be selected to meet a minimum of 55% of the calculated heat load of the building at a 55°C flow temperature, at design conditions.

sources.harvard: Western Power Distribution and Wales & West Utilities (2018) Freedom Project final report. October. Newport/Bristol: WPD and WWU (with PassivSystems, Imperial College London, Element Energy, Delta-ee). Available at: https://www.wwutilities.co.uk/media/2829/freedom-project-final-report-october-2018.pdf (accessed 7 November 2026).

claims.claim: 75 homes with hybrid heating systems deployed in Bridgend; predictive optimisation of running costs, contrasted with temperature-based fuel switching.
claims.quote: This is in stark contrast with traditional hybrid systems that simply switch fuel based on external temperature.

claims.claim: On mains gas, switching was economic rather than capacity-driven; 5 kW heat pumps sufficed for most homes.
claims.quote: For all homes on mains gas, fuel switching was determined economically (i.e. the boiler becomes a cheaper way of heating the house after a certain point), rather than because the heat pump no longer had enough heating capacity

claims.claim: Optimised hybrids achieved median SPF 3.60, because controls use the heat pump only when SPF is good enough.
claims.quote: PassivSystems hybridised heat pumps achieved significantly better SPFs (median 3.60 when optimised for current gas prices) than those of monovalent heat pumps in other trials

claims.claim: Grid-aware dispatch demonstrated: heat pump demand cut to <20 W per home within minutes, gas filling the gap, without comfort loss.
claims.quote: heat pump electricity demand can be reliably reduced to less than 20W per home within a few minutes if required, lasting indefinitely, without impacting occupant comfort.

claims.claim: Aggregate capping of 54 homes achieved to within 0.1-0.2 kW per home.
claims.quote: heat pump electricity demand can be managed to avoid increasing overall peak demand, to an accuracy of about 0.1 to 0.2 kW/home.

claims.claim: Predictive control trades fabric storage, extra losses and discomfort quantitatively.
claims.quote: Decisions are made on the basis of quantitative trade-offs between storing heat in the fabric of the building, the additional heat losses incurred and any discomfort for the occupants.
claims.locator: s.4.2 Demand response with predictive control, PDF p.25

claims.claim: Supervisory heat pump control divides into rule-based (RBC) and model predictive (MPC) strategies.
claims.quote: A distinction was drawn between rule-based controls (RBC) and model predictive controls (MPC), given the clear differences in their concept and complexity.

claims.claim: In MPC studies, cost minimisation dominates as the objective.
claims.quote: Notably in MPC, the monetary objective (reduction of the energy costs) has been the most utilized in the literature

claims.claim: Building thermal mass appears more cost-effective storage than water buffer tanks.
claims.quote: the built-in thermal mass seeming more cost-effective than water buffer tanks in this regard.

claims.claim: Formal definition: an overlay service over one or more underlays that recognises application flows and forwards by policy.
claims.quote: An overlay connectivity service that optimizes transport of IP Packets over one or more Underlay Connectivity Services by recognizing applications (Application Flows) and determining forwarding behavior by applying Policies to them.
claims.locator: s.3 Terminology and Abbreviations, entry SD-WAN Service

claims.claim: Continuous measurement and re-steering is the defining benefit.
claims.quote: The Service Provider monitors the performance of the available forwarding options and modifies how packets in each Application Flow are forwarded to achieve the desired behavior.

claims.claim: Disparate underlays with different cost and performance give cost, resilience and differentiated transport; cost is an explicit underlay attribute (flat-rate or usage-based).
claims.quote: Multiple Underlay Connectivity Services with different performance and cost characteristics (e.g., an IP-VPN over MPLS Network versus an Internet Access Service) can be used to provide cost benefits, resiliency, and differentiated transport.
claims.locator: section Underlay Connectivity Service, UCS UNI, and UCS End Point, pp.16-17

claims.claim: The standard defines externally visible service behaviour; the controller/orchestrator is outside normative scope.
claims.quote: This document does not include any normative information relating to: Management and orchestration of SD-WAN Services
